correctness.rationale: The dual contains exactly the subsets with no disconnected induced four-set. A separate verifier rebuilt it, found 429 disconnected quadruples and dual face counts (12,66,220,66,6), and verified all 66 supplied collapse pairs against the live complex. The remaining two-complex has counts (12,66,160) and is simply connected since the original dual has the complete two-skeleton. Its H_2 is free of rank 105 by Euler characteristic and freeness of the top cycle subgroup. Integral Hurewicz and homology Whitehead give the two-sphere wedge. Integral combinatorial Alexander duality on twelve vertices shifts to degree 9-j. The absence of six-element dual faces gives the full five-skeleton of K and hence four-connectivity; H_5=H_6=0 allows two more Hurewicz steps. K has dimension seven, so representatives of an H_7 basis give the other wedge by Whitehead. The two inner triangles determine the inner layer and the outer hexagon and spokes determine the full D_6. Oriented fixed-simplex traces in degree two of the dual reproduced both character rows. For transfer to K the inverse-action convention leaves the traces unchanged and the ambient sign is +1 because the layer actions are copies of the same permutation. Averaging gives 8. This establishes ordinary homotopy types and a homology representation, not an equivariant wedge.

value.rationale: The Dürer graph is a natural cubic benchmark with triangles, outside the cited pentagonal-girth and full-skeleton cases. The collapse gives an integral homotopy result stronger than finite-field ranks, and the character and invariant rank provide data for a symmetry action that the abstract wedge cannot recover.
